note: N. 4010.0 ± .3 in from the base centre, §64, the same point as 524.1 ± .3 in S. of the N. base edge. §35 gives that 524.1 ± .3 in, the probable error being that of fixing the length of the sides.
mid. 287.0 ± .8 in E. of the centre, §64; stated the same in §35, which adds 3723.6 in from the E. side and 4297.6 in from the W. side at that level.
+668.2 ± .1 in above the pavement, §64 and §35, reduced to the true beginning of the floor and not to the present broken entrance.
N. 306. ± 2. in, §64, with 4228. ± 2. in from the N. base edge. §36 derives it as 524.1 + 3704.3 = 4228 ± 2? or 306 N. from the mid-plane, with Petrie's own query mark and no ± on the 306.
mid. 286.4 ± 1. in E., §64. §36 derives it as 287.0 − [sin(3′55″ − 3′44″) × 3704] − .4 difference of offsets = 286.4 ± 1.0.
−1181. ± 1. in, §64. §36 derives it as 668.2 − (4140 × sin 26°31′23″) − .8 difference of floor offsets = −1181 ± 1?, with Petrie's own query mark.

S. 40. ± 2. in, §64, with 4574. ± 2. in from the N. base edge. §37 puts the large chamber's N. wall at 40 S. of the central axis, 346 in along the horizontal passage from the end of the entrance passage floor, so the axis passes 40 in inside the rock of the N. side.
mid. 286.3 ± 1. in E., §64; the same figure stands in §37's table, where the mid of the passage is read as an offset W. of the entrance axis continued, which runs at 286.8 E.

−1178. ± 1. in, §64. §37 tabulates roofs rather than floors: the roof of the horizontal passage at −1143 (top +38.3 above the entrance passage floor end) less the 35.5 E. and 36.0 W. height gives −1178.8.
S. 203. ± 2. in, §64, with 4737. ± 2. in from the N. base edge; the mid of §37's N. wall at 40 S. and S. wall at 366 S.
mid. 25.9 ± 2. in E., §64. §37's wall distances give (302.9 − 250.6)/2 = 26.2 at the N. wall and (299.6 − 254.5)/2 = 22.6 at the S. wall, mean 24.4, so §64's 25.9 is not simply their mean.

−1056. ± 2. in, §64, which is the roof and not the floor: §37 gives the large chamber top at +125.3 above the entrance passage floor end, its note 4 adding +124.3 at the N. doorway and 125.4 to 127.6 at the S. The floor was never finished, running 140 below the roof over the flat eastern part, 155 on a knob beside the shaft and 198 at the best worked surface.

553.5 in E. to W. at the N. wall, §37, from the line under the table: Large Chamber, E. Wall 325.9; at 100 from West. Wall 329.6?; N. Wall 553.5; S. Wall 554.1. It agrees with the wall distances from the central axis given just below, 302.9 E. and 250.6 W. at the N. wall. No error stated for the figure itself; §37 estimates the average irregularity of the walls at ± .7 and the chamber is plainly unfinished.
554.1 in E. to W. at the S. wall, §37, the same line, agreeing with 299.6 E. and 254.5 W. at the S. wall. No error stated.
325.9 in N. to S. along the E. wall, §37, the same line, agreeing with the N. wall at 40 S. and the S. wall at 366 S. of the central axis. No error stated.

329.6 in N. to S. measured at 100 in from the W. end, §37, with Petrie’s own query mark: the W. side could not be reached without clearing the fallen stone, and he calls the measure perhaps somewhat askew. No error stated.

140 in below the roof, §37, over the lower eastern part of the floor, which is comparatively flat. The floor was never finished, so the same section gives 155 in below the roof on a knob of rock beside the shaft and 198 in at the best worked surface around it, and estimates the roof’s average variation at ± 3. No error stated for the 140.
S. 366. ± 2. in, §64, with 4900. ± 2. in from the N. base edge; the large chamber's S. wall in §37.
mid. 284.9 ± 1. in E., §64, as in §37's table, 1.9 W. of the entrance axis continued.
−1219. ± 1.5 in, §64. §37 gives the roof at −1188 (top −6.6) and the height as 31.0 + x, so the floor is −1219.

S. 1012. in, §64, with 5546. ± 3. in from the N. base edge; the end of the rough southern drift-way in §37. §64 prints ± .3 in the From Centre column but ± 3. in the From N. Base column for the same point, and every other subterranean row carries ± 2 in both, so the ± .3 is taken as a misprint and the ± 3 used.
mid. 277.1 in E., §64, as in §37's table, 9.7 W. of the entrance axis continued. No error stated in either place.
−1213. ± 2. in, §64. §37 gives the roof at −1184 (top −2.6) and the height as 29.5 E. and 29.3 W., so the floor is −1213.4.

31.6 to 33.3 in, §37, the width E. to W. of the horizontal subterranean passage: the table gives 32.9, then top and base pairs of 32.3 and 32.4, 31.6 and 32.7, 31.9 and 33.0, and 32.0 and 33.3. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it. The flat end of the entrance passage above it is 40.8 wide, and the rough southern drift-way beyond the chamber is narrower, 26.0 to 30.1 in the same table, so this record does not describe either of them.

35.5 on the E. and 36.0 on the W., §37, the height of the horizontal passage out of the end of the entrance passage; the passage is horizontal, so its perpendicular and vertical heights are the same. Stored as the mid of the two readings with sigma covering them. The rest of §37’s height column reads 48.5 at the flat end of the entrance passage, 31.0 + x where the floor could not be reached, and 26.0 to 29.5 in the southern drift-way.

N. 3016.3 ± .3 in, §64, with 1517.8 ± .3 in from the N. base edge. §38 fixes the point where the ascending floor produced cuts the entrance floor at 1110.64 ± .1 in along the entrance floor from the casing face.
mid. 286.6 ± .8 in E., §64. §38 does not restate it; it follows from the entrance passage mid of 287.0 ± .8 in §35 carried 1110.64 in down the slope.

172.9 in above the pavement. §39 uses that figure explicitly, (172.9 + 679.7) = 852.6 for the level of the passage's upper end, and 668.2 − 1110.64 × sin 26°31′23″ from §35 and §38 gives 172.2 before the floor offset corrections. The §64 cell reads + 179.9 ± .2, which is 7 in too high to be reconciled with either, so the 9 is read as a corrupted 2 and §39's 172.9 stored; ± .2 as printed in §64.
N. 1626.8 ± .8 in, §64 and §39, at the latitude of the E. wall of the gallery. §39 puts the same point 2907.3 ± .6 in from the N. base edge; §64 prints ± .8 for that cell.
mid. 287. ± 1.5 in E., §64 and §39. The azimuth of the passage, −4′ ± 3′, is so close to that of the Pyramid side that §39 assumes it parallel.
+852.6 in above the pavement, §64 with ± .3. §39 gives it as (172.9 + 679.7) = 852.6 ± 3, which must be a misprint for ± .3 since §40's table repeats 852.6 ± .3.

41.6 in, §38: the granite plugs are 38.2 wide at the lower end “in place of 41.6 at the upper end”, the passage contracting so that the plugs jam. §39 says the passage's own width and height cannot be measured, the surfaces being so decayed that opposite original faces survive only at the ends. No error stated.

47.3 in perpendicular to the floor, §38: the plug height is “unaltered, being at lower end 47.30 E., 47.15 mid, 47.26 W.; and at upper, or S. end 47.3”. §38 states the pyramid's passages as 47 perpendicularly or 52 vertically. No error stated.

41.6 in, §38, which gives 41.6 as the breadth of the passage the plugs fit and of the trial passages that copy the entrance passage, before their contraction to 38.0 and 37.5. §35 and §36 state no mean width for the entrance passage itself: §36 gives only offsets from the mean axis, W. 20.4 to 21.6 and E. 20.5 to 21.3, mean error .23. No error stated.

47 in perpendicular to the floor, §38: “the passages of the Pyramid, which are 47 perpendicularly or 52 vertically”. §36 gives only offsets from the mean axis, roof +23.2 to +24.3 and floor −23.3 to −24.9, mean error .30, and states no mean height for the entrance passage. No error stated.

N. 102.0 ± .8 in, §64 and §40's table (chamber N. wall, side of door). §64's From N. Base cell reads 4402.1 ± .8, but every other row of that table is 4534.1 in from the N. base edge less the From Centre figure, which gives 4432.1 here, so the printed 4402.1 looks like a typo.

side 308. ± 3. in E. of the centre, §64, the chamber's E. wall. Nothing in §41 or §42 places the chamber east or west, and 308 is hard to reconcile with the rest: it leaves 236 in to §64's “side 72.” for the mid W. roof against §41's mean W. wall to E. wall of 226.47 in, and it puts the E. wall only 21 in E. of the 287 ± 3 in axis §40 gives the passage that enters the N. wall. The least trustworthy pair of figures in §64.
+834.4 in above the pavement, §64 with ± .4; §40's table gives the same 834.4 with ± .3 for the chamber floor at the N. wall.
N. .3 ± .8 in, §64. §41 says the ridge of the roof is in the mid-plane of the Pyramid within the probable error of the determination, and §46 states the measure as .3 ± .8 N.
side 72. ± 3. in E. of the centre, §64, the chamber's W. wall. See qc.corner.ne.east: 308 − 72 = 236 against §41's 226.47 in mean length W. wall to E. wall.

+1078.7 ± .6 in above the pavement, §64, marked “roof”; the apex of the gable at the W. wall. §40's table gives the chamber's E. apex at 1080.1 with no error stated, so the ridge falls 1.4 in from E. to W.

184.47 in high on the N. and S. walls, §41, in the same sentence as the 205.85 wide, 226.47 long and 245.1 high to the top of the roof ridge on the E. and W. walls. Heights are reckoned from the footing of fine stone at the base of the walls, §42, the general floor being unfinished core masonry. No error stated.

S. 61.7 in, §64 with ± .9 and §45 with ± .8, and 4595.8 ± .9 in from the N. base edge. The virtual floor end is where the general floor slope, carried on through the step, would intersect the plane of the S. wall (§64 note 9).
mid. 284.4 in E., §64 with ± 3. and §45 with ± 2.8, reckoned continuously through from the plug-blocks upwards.
+1689.0 ± .5 in above the pavement, §64 and §45.
S. .4 in, §64 with ± .9 and §46 with ± .8, the latter as (61.7 − 61.3). §46 reads the face of the step as the transit from the northern to the southern half of the Pyramid.
mid. 284.4 ± 3. in E., §64, the same as the gallery floor's virtual S. end.

+1694.1 ± .7 in above the pavement, §64. §47's table gives the face of the step at 1693.7 to 1694.6 ± .6, whose mid is 1694.15; §46 works the step surface at the E. side of the S. doorway out separately as 1693.2 ± .6.
S. 113.7 ± .9 in, §64 and §47's table, at 52.02 in along the floor from the S. wall of the gallery; 4647.8 ± .9 in from the N. base edge.
§64 gives only “same ?” in the E. from Centre column, that is the same as the two gallery rows above it, mid. 284.4 ± 3., with Petrie's own query mark. Stored at that value and that error.
+1692.6 ± .6 in above the pavement, §64; §47's table gives the two readings 1692.6 and 1692.9 at ± .6.
S. 229.8 ± .9 in, §64 and §47's table, at 168.10 in along the floor from the S. wall of the gallery; 4763.9 ± .9 in from the N. base edge.
§64 gives only “same ?” in the E. from Centre column, that is mid. 284.4 ± 3. carried down from the gallery rows, with Petrie's own query mark.

+1841.5 ± .6 in above the pavement, §64, marked “roof”. §48 works the same ceiling out as 152.85 ± .2 over the virtual end of the gallery floor and 1841.8 ± .6 over the pavement, so the two differ by .3 in.

1883.6 in on the slope, §45, from the N. wall of the gallery to the S. wall in the same line. §46 uses the same figure: 1883.6 × cos 26°16′40″ = 1688.9 horizontal, from which it takes the roof length as 1648.4 horizontal or 1838.6 sloping. No error stated.

26°16′40″, §45, the mean axis in altitude to which the gallery offsets are reduced; the azimuth of the same axis is +1′20″. §39 gives 26°12′50″ for the ascending passage and the gallery taken together as one length. No error stated.

41.1 in between the ramps. §46 gives the width of the top of the gallery as 40.9 at N. and 41.3 at S., and states that “the space between the ramps (2 cubits), is equal to the space between the walls at the top”. Sigma is half the N. to S. spread; no error stated.

20.55 in. §46 measures the seven lap projections by plumb-line at 20.50 on the E. and 20.40 on the W., 20.9 on the S. end and 20.4 on the N., “mean of all, 20.55, for the sum of the seven projections of the laps, or one cubit”, and says “the laps overhang the ramps along the gallery sides”. Petrie states 20.55 as the overhang, not as a direct measure of the ramp. No error stated.

Seven. §46, from the plumb-line measures at the S. end: mean of all, 20.55, for the sum of the seven projections of the laps, or one cubit, the laps being then one palm each in breadth. The lap table in the same section numbers eight laps, the topmost cut away by Vyse’s forced hole and only supposed to project 3 in like the others, so the seven projections are the seven steps of overhang between them.

33.0 to 34.0 in, §46’s High on S. End column, which reads 33.6, 33.7, 33.0, 34.0 and 33.8 for the laps of stone that corbel the gallery walls inward. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it. §46 gives no lap heights at the N. end, where Vyse’s forced hole cut the top lap away.

2.3, 3.1, 3.0 and 2.9 in, §46’s Lap on W. side column, the overhang of one lap. Stored as the mid of that range with sigma covering it. §46 adds that the top lap was so entirely cut away by Vyse’s hole that Petrie could only suppose it to project 3 inches, like the others, and that the seven projections together measure 20.55, or one cubit, the laps being then one palm each in breadth.

166.2 ± .8 in vertically above the gallery floor, §46, Prof. Smyth’s mean height of the third lap, quoted by Petrie and not measured by him; the groove in the lower part of that lap then runs 172.1 to 179.0 over the floor. This is the only lap that §46 places above the floor: it states no height for the first lap over the ramps or the floor, so none is stored.

40.9 at the N. and 41.3 at the S. end, §46, the width of the top of the gallery. Stored as the mid with sigma covering the two readings. §46 states that the space between the ramps, 2 cubits, is equal to the space between the walls at the top, which is why gg.floor.width carries the same 41.1.

339 in, the mid of 334 to 344. §46: Prof. Smyth's mean height of the third lap above the gallery floor is 166.2 ± .8 vertically, so the groove runs 172.1 to 179.0 over the floor and “its lower edge is therefore at half the height of the gallery, that varying from 167 to 172”. Sigma is half the 334 to 344 range; Petrie states no ± on the height itself.
116.30 in N. to S., §48, the mean of the two series from top to base above the granite wainscot; the individual readings run 114.07 to 117.00. No error stated.
65.00 in E. to W., §48, above the granite wainscot; the individual readings run 64.48 to 65.48. No error stated.
149.35 in, §48, the mean of the five stations from near the N. wall to the S. wall; §48 adds that this puts the ceiling 152.85 ± .2 over the virtual end of the gallery floor. No error stated.
S. 330.6 in, §64 with ± .9 and §55 with ± .8, the N. wall at its base; 4864.7 ± .9 in from the N. base edge.
S. 537.0 ± .8 in, §55; §64's summary has no S. wall row. 537.0 − 330.6 = 206.4, against the 206.12 ± .12 mean width of §155 and the 206.29 E. and 205.97 W. of §52.
side 305.0 ± 3. in E. of the centre, §64; §55 gives (284.4 ± 20.7) = 305.1 ± 3.0. The §64 value is stored and the .1 in difference noted.
107.7 ± 3.0 in W. of the centre, §55; §64's summary has no W. wall row. 305.1 + 107.7 = 412.8, against the 412.24 ± .12 mean length of §155.
1922.65 in above the pavement, the mid of the 1921.6 to 1923.7 ± .6 range that both §55 and §64 give for the ceiling. Sigma is half the 2.1 in range plus Petrie's ± .6.

1692.55 in above the pavement, the mid of the 1691.4 to 1693.7 ± .6 range §55 gives for the actual floor; sigma is half the 2.3 in range plus Petrie's ± .6. §54 explains the spread: the floor is disconnected from the walls and its depth below the first course joint varies 2.29, from 42.94 to 40.65. §64's single-point figure for the King's Chamber floor is +1692.8 ± .6, which is §47's raised floor at the passage end; §55 puts the base of the walls at 1686.3 to 1688.5 ± .6.

89.62 in N. to S. outside, §59 (p. 86), between the mean planes of the N. and S. ends. The example under the table puts the actual E. side at 90.01 half way up, 90.14 at 8 in under the top and 90.29 at 4 in above the bottom; the coffer's long axis runs N. and S., as §58's wall distances show.
38.50 in E. to W. outside, §59, between the mean planes of the E. and W. sides.
41.31 in, §59, the outer height; the base is 6.89 thick.
78.06 in, §59, with the N. end 5.67 and the S. end 5.89 thick.
26.81 in, §59, with the E. side 5.87 and the W. side 5.82 thick.
34.42 in, §59; the ledge the lid slid into is 1.70 deep, cut along the N., E. and S. sides with the W. side cut down to it.
53.32 in at the base (53.34 at the top), §58, from the coffer's N.W. corner to the W. wall, as it stood on the floor tilted up at the S. end by a flint pebble.
56.54 in at the base (56.50 at the top), §58, S.W. corner to the W. wall: the coffer is not square to the chamber, its W. side 3.2 in further from the wall at the S. end.
50.06 in at the base (48.90 at the top), §58, N.W. corner to the N. wall; the N.E. corner stands 48.35 at the base and 47.70 at the top from it.
41.07 in, the mean depth from back to front in §43's table; §43 says the original depth back was only 41 in at every part, the deeper hole behind being a broken joint of masonry.

25.19 in, the mean of §43's column from the plumb-line below the apex of the roof to the middle of the niche, every tier reading 25.1 to 25.3 S.: the niche stands that far south of the chamber's mid-line, in the E. wall.
183.8 in above the floor, §43, where the niche is roofed across (184 in the text).
61.74 in, §43's mean width of the lowest tier, from the floor to 67.14 in; the text's 62 in, 3 cubits.
52.74 in, §43, the second tier, 67.14 to 98.93 in above the floor.
41.83 in, §43, the third tier, 98.93 to 127.16 in.
30.43 in, §43, the fourth tier, 127.16 to 156.10 in.
20.30 in, §43, the top tier, 156.10 to 183.8 in; the text's 20 in, 1 cubit.
67.14 in above the floor, §43, the first overlapping of the niche's sides, at a wall course.
98.93 in, §43, the second overlapping.
127.16 in, §43, the third overlapping.
156.10 in, §43, the fourth overlapping.
155 in below the roof on a knob of rock beside the shaft (the pit), §37, in the same passage as the 140 in of chamber.subterranean.height over the flat eastern part.
198 in below the roof at the best worked surface round the shaft (the pit), §37, the same passage; the floor was never finished.
